text:
morgan: FYI ran the weekly perf sweep on an 8xA100 cluster with the new KV-shard async coalesce patch and hit a 10-15% throughput regression on TP+PP configs. details below. :frown:
sara: ouch. which model/config?
morgan: Redwood-13B, seq_len=1024, TP=2 PP=4 (pipeline stages interleaved), DP=1. baseline (sync all-reduce) = 12.3k tok/s, new async coalesce = 10.6k tok/s.
jamie: do you have traces from nvprof / CUPTI? where is the time going (all-reduce vs kernel time vs stall)? :eyes:
morgan: attached sampling from perf-bot: "kernel_time: 45ms, allreduce_wait: 18ms, idle_wait: 9ms" (percentiles averaged across steps). Seems all-reduce latency spiked and we lost overlap.
mo: async coalesce reduced the number of small allreduces but increased tail latency because we coalesced across layers that would have overlapped compute earlier. tradeoff turned negative with our scheduling.
tina: timeline theory: we were relying on intra-stage compute to hide small allreduces. coalescing pushed them into a single bigger barrier that stalls the pipeline.
sara: can you paste the profiler flame? just a tiny snippet is fine.
morgan: sure — snippet from perf-bot trace:```
Step 1234:
  stage0 compute  (kernel)  12.4ms
  kv-prefetch (async)      2.1ms
  allreduce coalesced      9.8ms  <-- used to be ~2.3ms x4 overlapped
  stage1 compute  (kernel) 10.9ms
```
jamie: that allreduce line is the culprit. previously we had 4 small reduces amortized under compute. coalescing helped bandwidth but removed concurrency.
mo: two quick experiment ideas: (1) selective coalesce: only coalesce if tiny reduces are on the critical path and compute slack < threshold. (2) aggressive kernel fusion + lower-latency kernel path to shorten compute so reduces fit back into overlap.
tina: +1 on selective policy. also consider sharding KV differently: current TP-aligned KV shard puts many cold keys on same GPU so prefetch bursts cause synchronized reduces. maybe try round-robin slicing across PP stages.
morgan: I ran a quick ablation — switched KV sharding from "per-tensor TP affinity" to "stripe across PP stages" and saw allreduce_wait drop from 18ms -> 8.5ms, throughput up ~6%. but latency p50 increased slightly (from 38ms -> 42ms).
\amsg (perf-bot): auto-checkpoint: nightly-run 2145006000 detected throughput_regression=12%. attached flame and topk ops.
sara: interesting. tradeoff looks promising. what about memory pressure / KV cache occupancy?
morgan: occupancy stayed within limits; memory delta ~+1.8GB due to more KV replicas in the stripe scheme (we replicate some hot entries to avoid fetchs).
jamie: if replication helps overlap, might be worth it. we should quantify cost impact (tokens/$).
mo: note on kernel selection: the combined changes interacted with a less-optimized matmul kernel we recently promoted for int8 paths. that kernel's lower throughput reduced compute slack further, making coalescing worse.
tina: oh right, kernel rollout 2139999000 — we saw a small regression on int8 earlier. can we toggle kernel back-to-old for experiment?
morgan: did that — with old kernel + stripe KV + selective coalesce we recovered baseline and gained +3% throughput.
sara: nice. so plan: (A) roll back the new matmul kernel on TP+PP until we finish tuning, (B) implement selective coalesce heuristic (compute slack threshold + per-layer hotness check), (C) prototype KV stripe sharding with optional hot-entry replication and measure cost impact.
jamie: I'll open a PR with the heuristic sketch and perf test harness. can we have a small canary on dedicated cluster? @deploy-bot can you schedule a canary job? :rocket:
deploy-bot: scheduling canary job: redwood-ci/canary/kvshard-2145006789 on dedicated-gpu-3, ETA 14m.
mo: also add a kernel fallback toggle so we can A/B kernel selection per-run. we need better telemetry to know when a kernel reduces compute slack below threshold.
morgan: agreed. I'll add a telemetry metric: compute_slack_ms per-step and expose it on the per-route dashboard.
sara: leave a note in the release channel when you've validated. also add perf-eval prompt sets for regression catches.
morgan: will do. thanks all. :thumbsup:
jamie: quick todo list in-thread: 1) PR heuristic (jamie) 2) KV stripe prototype + cost calc (morgan) 3) canary runs + telemetry (mo/tina) 4) kernel A/B toggle (jamie). target to close in 3 days.
sara: great. ping me if the canary shows any regressions.
perf-bot: run-complete: redwood-ci/canary/kvshard-2145006789 -> success (throughput +2% vs baseline after combined changes).
morgan: sweet, closing the loop. we'll iterate on thresholds next week.
